protocol.primary: Paired mean correct private-key bits: frozen ridge prediction minus independent random baseline.
secondary: Paired mean key-bit benefit from choosing the more similar address of two candidates.
Mean changed address bits after one private-key bit flip; reference 80/160.
protocol.inference: Per-trial paired two-sided Student-t 95% CI; no treating 256 bits as independent subjects. Holm-adjusted p values across the three contrasts. No outcome-driven stopping.
protocol.fixedStop: Exactly 2000, 2000 and 512 fresh trials. No model training, weight updates or target-wallet input.
protocol.exclusion: Only a candidate scalar outside 1 <= k < secp256k1 order is rejected by deterministic rejection sampling.
protocol.timing: Fresh and replay wall-clock UTC and monotonic elapsed times plus process CPU time are recorded. Original per-trial times are unavailable.
protocol.evidence: Original deterministic replay is a reproducibility check, not a fresh replication. Fresh cohort uses a seed drawn after freezing current model files. The protocol is internally timestamped, not externally preregistered.
protocol.privacy: Synthetic private keys exist only in process memory and are never written. No wallet balance/network requests. Public observation contains only aggregate Hamming-distance statistics.
limitations: Original training keys are unavailable; explicit training/holdout set-overlap cannot be audited. Fresh seed generation is independent of the frozen training process.
Original individual rows and timestamps were not recorded; reconstructed rows must not be presented as original logs.
Observational point-stream samples are not controlled AI trials and will not be pooled with them.
Statistical consistency with randomness is not proof of cryptographic security or impossibility of future methods.

modelMetadata.input: 160 Ethereum address bits, MSB first; no checksum case

observation.scope: Exploratory public-address statistics; iid/binomial reference is an explicit model assumption, not demonstrated cryptographic independence.

limitations: Measured op counts are group additions/doublings, not equivalent CPU instructions.
Memory/operation caps cause SKIPPED or CAPPED, not failures of attacks.
ML is kNN scalar regression on (x/p,y/p), disjoint training and test keys.
ML accuracy 1/n is a theoretical uniform-guess baseline; 60 trials per curve cannot resolve such tiny probabilities.
Positive MOV test is on a weak supersingular curve; it does not imply the ML model learned the attack.
Theoretical projections are not observed timings.

limitations: 36-bit rho cap is 160 000 group operations, below the expected ~1.25*sqrt(n) ≈ 290 000; heavy censoring there is by design, not a method failure.
24-bit exhaustive: independent random secrets but correlated shared-prefix timing, not independent CPU timings.
Brute force time estimates are not comparable with separately timed rho / BSGS.
rho20 counts preprocessing group operations; walk_steps are separate.
Floyd rho3 baseline counts total group operations including 3 walk updates per comparison; old code does not expose exact walk steps.
Failed/capped trials are right censored and MUST NOT be treated as exact completion.
KM median is undefined where survival never falls to 50%.
ML classifier uses both normalized public X and Y and 5-NN bitwise majority, plus majority bit and random exact key baselines.
No support for a cryptographic breakthrough.
Automorphism identity and orbit sizes are mathematically known, NOT newly discovered.
Collision sampling is independent random drawing from a mathematical quotient, NOT a functioning Pollard rho ECDLP search.
Sample-count gain ignores canonicalization costs, fruitless cycles, validation and search setup.
Actual speedup of a real walk may be smaller or absent; no attack on Ethereum keys or addresses was performed.
Small research curves share j=0 symmetry but do not reproduce the 256-bit security setting.
No ML model or novel learning shortcut was tested in this study.
